newsitem.title: FRANCE: French FM to visit Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan.
newsitem.headline: French FM to visit Turkey, Armenia, Azerbaijan.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette flies to Azerbaijan and Armenia this week in an effort to mediate in their dispute over Nagorno-Karabakh.

He will also visit Ankara to try to assuage fears that the European Union has turned its back on Turkey after a number of Christian Democrat EU leaders appeared two weeks ago to rule out its bid for membership.
Officials in Paris said de Charette's trip to Baku on Tuesday and Erevan on Wednesday would highlight France's commitment to negotiations over the disputed Armenian enclave in Azerbaijan.

Moslem Azerbaijan and Christian Armenia have been at odds for nine years over the disputed territory, the Armenian population of which fought for years against rule by Baku. Thousands were killed until a ceasefire was agreed in 1994.

President Haydar Aliyev of Azerbaijan welcomed French mediation efforts when he met President Jacques Chirac last week, on his way to Moscow for a summit of former Soviet republics and talks with Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan.

De Charette said after meeting Aliyev that the problem of Nagorno-Karabakh was a priority. He said Paris, Moscow and Washington, the co-chairmen of the Minsk group mandated by the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) to seek a solution to the conflict, were united in their determination to find an equitable settlement soon.
In Ankara on Thursday, de Charette will try to persuade Turkey that its bid for EU membership is still alive despite the hostile comments made at the Christian Democrat meeting.
Paris has distanced itself from the criticism. French diplomats say that anchoring Turkey in Europe is a priority and a condition for the prosperity and stability of the whole region.

De Charette was expected to tell Ankara that Turkey's place was in the European Union, but that it must first adhere to the EU rules of democracy and human rights and settle its disputes with Greece to establish good neighbourly relations.
